metadata.location: Krayan Selatan, Nunukan, North Kalimantan, Indonesia
metadata.note: Official BNPB publication time is used as the conservative public decision cutoff. The packet tests whether an established access-to-fuel-to-power dependency is diagnosed without inventing independent power-capacity scarcity.

evidence_manifest.notes: BNPB field update attributes the road/bridge isolation, stopped fuel-truck operation and reduced generator electricity hours to current local response reporting. It is not a complete live capability inventory.

metadata.claim_boundary: Official condition evidence establishes the road/bridge closure and its disruption of fuel delivery to the generator. It does not establish that all alternative transport, fuel or power capability is absent.

needs.location_ref: Krayan Barat-Krayan Selatan corridor, Nunukan, Indonesia
needs.notes: BNPB reported the main road closed by landslide material and the connecting bridge impassable, isolating 13 villages.
BNPB reported electricity availability reduced from about 12 hours to four hours per day because fuel distribution to the power generator was disrupted.

dependencies.notes: The same official update states that fuel-transport vehicles could not operate and attributes reduced electricity hours to disrupted fuel distribution.

reference.historical_action: By 24-25 July BNPB used pioneer aircraft to move relief into the still-isolated area while continuing coordination to reopen the road and repair the damaged bridge.
reference.historical_outcome_summary: The later response demonstrates that alternative logistics can emerge while the road dependency remains broken. It supports dependency-aware workaround reasoning but does not establish that power service was restored or that the replay recommendation caused a better outcome.
notes: The later BNPB air-relief report is hidden from the decision payload.
The replay must identify the upstream access dependency without promoting unknown alternative power/logistics capability into either scarcity or deployability.
